confirmed.label: Confirmed
confirmed.explain: A court, coroner, regulator or accident investigator found that the system caused or contributed to the death.

alleged.label: Confirmed or alleged
alleged.explain: Adds deaths blamed on a named AI system in a lawsuit, an open investigation, or reporting by at least two news organisations. Not established.

listed.label: Everything any list has
listed.explain: The largest count this page could assemble: Wikipedia's chatbot list (39), every Autopilot or FSD death on tesladeaths.com (65), plus Uber (1), openpilot (2) and nH Predict (1).

annual.name: Tobacco
annual.note: WHO puts the toll at over seven million deaths a year. Older WHO material says eight million, counting 1.2 to 1.3 million non-smokers.

annual.name: Alcohol
annual.note: 4.7% of all deaths that year. Two million of the dead were men.

src.label: WHO global status report on alcohol and health, 2024

annual.name: Cars
annual.note: More than half the dead were not in a car: 23% were pedestrians, 21% riders of motorcycles and three-wheelers, 6% cyclists. Down 5% since 2010.

src.label: WHO global status report on road safety 2023

annual.name: Gravity
annual.note: The second-largest cause of unintentional injury death, after road traffic. Excludes falls from animals, vehicles and burning buildings.

annual.name: Mosquitoes
annual.note: Malaria only; dengue and other mosquito-borne diseases would add to it. Most of the dead were young children in Africa.

annual.name: Water
annual.note: About 30 people an hour. The death rate has fallen 38% since 2000.

src.label: WHO global status report on drowning prevention 2024

annual.name: Guns
annual.note: Uncertainty interval 195,000 to 276,000. 64% homicides, 27% suicides, 9% accidents. Six countries account for half.

src.label: Global Burden of Disease 2016 Injury Collaborators, JAMA 2018

annual.name: Snakes
annual.note: WHO says the data are fragmented and the true toll could be anywhere in this range.

annual.name: Knives
annual.sub: homicides with knives and sharp objects
annual.note: About a fifth of the 464,000 homicides the UN counted that year. Homicides only, so this row is an undercount next to Guns, which includes suicides and accidents.

annual.name: Dogs
annual.sub: rabies, 99% of it from dog bites
annual.note: WHO calls this figure a likely underestimate. Four in ten of the dead are children under 15.

annual.name: Selfies
annual.note: 259 deaths in news reports from October 2011 to November 2017, about 42 a year, peaking at 98 in 2016. The authors say it is an undercount.

src.label: Bansal et al., J Family Med Prim Care 2018, as reported by CBS

annual.name: AI
annual.note: Deaths dated 2025 that someone has blamed on a chatbot: 14 on hasaikilledanyone.com, 20 on Wikipedia's list. None is confirmed by an official finding. Driver-assist crashes are left out because no source gives a clean 2025 count; adding every Autopilot or FSD death any tracker has ever recorded (65) would bring this row to 85.

annual.name: Sharks
annual.note: Twelve shark-related deaths in 2025, nine of them from unprovoked bites. The ten-year average for unprovoked deaths is six.

alltime.name: AI, as forecast
alltime.sub: 5% chance × 8.2 billion people; not a count
alltime.note: In a 2023 survey of 2,778 AI researchers, the median respondent put a 5% chance on AI causing human extinction or similarly severe, permanent disempowerment. Multiply that by the world's population and the expected value tops this board. It is a forecast multiplied by a headcount. Nobody on this row has died.

src.label: AI Impacts: 2023 expert survey, methodology FAQ
IEEE Spectrum on the survey and its critics

alltime.name: Smallpox
alltime.note: State of the art. An estimated 300 million deaths in the 20th century alone. Declared eradicated in 1980 and no longer maintained.

src.label: Origins (Ohio State): WHO and the end of smallpox

alltime.name: Tobacco
alltime.note: WHO's estimate for the last century. Its projection for this one, on current trends, is a billion.

src.label: WHO figures as reported by AFP/Rappler

alltime.name: Mao Zedong
alltime.sub: human baseline; Great Leap Forward famine
alltime.note: Estimates of famine deaths run from 15 to 55 million; Frank Dikötter's archival study argues for at least 45 million. Historians disagree on how to divide blame between policy and weather, though the Party's own 1981 verdict put it mainly on the Great Leap Forward. Other campaigns are not counted here.

alltime.name: Adolf Hitler
alltime.sub: human baseline; murdered by the Nazi regime
alltime.note: About 17 million people murdered by the Nazi regime and its collaborators, six million of them Jews. The total sums the US Holocaust Memorial Museum's estimates by group. It leaves out the rest of the 70 to 85 million who died in the Second World War.

src.label: Statista chart of the USHMM figures

alltime.name: Joseph Stalin
alltime.note: Since the Soviet archives opened, estimates cluster at six to nine million including famine deaths (Timothy Snyder's count). Cold War estimates of 20 million or more are still cited. Soviet war dead are not included.

src.label: Wikipedia: Excess mortality under Joseph Stalin

alltime.name: Pol Pot
alltime.note: Ben Kiernan's widely used figure is about 1.7 million, more than a fifth of the country in under four years. Demographer Patrick Heuveline's range is 1.2 to 2.8 million.

alltime.name: Atomic bombs
alltime.note: The credible estimates cluster at a low of 110,000 and a high of 210,000 for Hiroshima and Nagasaki together. On 5 August 1945 this row read zero.

src.label: Alex Wellerstein, Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists

alltime.name: Boeing MCAS
alltime.sub: ordinary software, not AI; two 737 MAX crashes
alltime.note: Lion Air 610 (189 dead) and Ethiopian Airlines 302 (157 dead). Rule-based software acting on one faulty sensor. Listed to show what plain automation has already done; it is not part of AI's total.

alltime.name: Selfies
alltime.note: 137 incidents in six years of English-language news reports. Drowning, transport and falls lead.

src.label: Bansal et al. 2018, as reported by CBS

alltime.name: AI
alltime.note: Five deaths confirmed by an official finding (four involving Tesla Autopilot, one an Uber test vehicle). Another 39 alleged in lawsuits, investigations or reporting. Counting everything any tracker lists gives 108. Use the control above the boards to switch rules.

alltime.name: Industrial robots
alltime.sub: ordinary automation, not AI; US only
alltime.note: A NIOSH search of US workplace fatality records. 78% involved a robot striking a worker, often during maintenance. One country only.

src.label: Layne, Am J Ind Med 2023 (CDC Stacks)

systems.other: 57 in crash reports to NHTSA; 65 on tesladeaths.com
No death count can be attributed
